title: Stability Prober for Multi-SLO Rollback Tuning
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We rely on hard thresholds (static windows and fixed deltas) to trigger automated rollback during canary and A/B rollouts. This causes two classes of failures: 1) noisy but transient spikes cause unnecessary rollbacks; 2) slow degradations of subtle cost/throughput trade-offs (e.g., token cost increases while latency stays within nominal bands) evade detection until customer impact is high.

Proposal: Build a "Stability Prober" component and tuning heuristic that (a) actively probes candidate deployments with lightweight synthetic/cohort traffic, (b) computes per-cohort baselines and bootstrapped confidence intervals across multiple SLO signals (p99 latency, error rate, token cost per 1k tokens, and throughput), and (c) derives an adaptive rollback trigger that combines hysteresis, progressive delay ramps, and cost-normalized scoring. Key ideas: compute short-term and longer-term baselines per region/customer-cohort; use bootstrapped quantiles to estimate uncertainty; require multi-signal agreement (weighted fusion) before triggering an automated rollback; apply an adaptive holdback (cooldown elasticity) whose length increases with uncertainty and with the magnitude of cost trade-offs.

Why this is different: existing heuristics use single-window detection or fixed step thresholds. The Stability Prober treats rollback as a safety choreography: probe traffic to increase signal-to-noise, bias toward manual review when signals conflict, and let the automatic path handle clear, high-confidence regressions quickly. Also we explicitly include token-cost as a first-class signal and normalize other metrics to a unit-economics band so rollbacks consider business impact, not just metric deltas.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prober service can generate synthetic probe requests (configurable size, prompt template, and user-cohort headers) and collect per-request metrics into the rollout telemetry pipeline.
- Baseline calculator implemented: computes bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals for each metric per cohort and stores recent baseline snapshots.
- Trigger evaluator implements weighted fusion across signals, hysteresis window, and adaptive cooldown ramp; exposes a read-only API for simulated rollouts.
- Runbook & playbook: documented manual override, canary inspector UI entries, and dashboard panels for probe traffic, baseline drift, and trigger explanations.
- Unit + integration tests for prober traffic handling, baseline stability under noise, and trigger decision logic (simulated signals).
- Successful smoke run: evaluate against 3 recent rollouts (one real canary incident and two synthetic scenarios) in staging and show reduction in false-positive rollbacks and faster detection of cost regressions.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Probe volume: needs to be low enough to avoid cost/noise but high enough to reduce measurement variance. We'll start with 0.5%-1% of canary traffic per cohort with decaying frequency.
- Signal fusion weights: initial weights = {latency:0.35, errors:0.35, cost:0.2, throughput:0.1}, tunable via console. We prioritize latency/errors but allow cost to veto slow degradations.
- Hysteresis windows: two-tier hysteresis (short 5min window for clear failures, long 30min window when signals are noisy). Adaptive cooldown extends the long window up to 4 hours for high-uncertainty cohorts.
- Cohort baselines: use 24h historical window + recent 30m window for drift detection. For new cohorts with insufficient history, bootstrap from similar cohorts and increase cooldown.
- Safety: manual abort always allowed; any automated rollback posts an explanation and a confidence score to the incident timeline.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prober microservice + SDK hooks (2 sprints): generate probes, tag telemetry, and write probe-level metrics to rollout topic.
2) Baseline service (1 sprint): bootstrap per-cohort baselines and CI computation.
3) Trigger evaluator (1 sprint): implement fusion engine, hysteresis, and adaptive cooldown. Start as simulation-only mode.
4) Console integration & runbook (1 sprint): show probe streams and decision explanations; add manual controls.
5) Staging run & tuning (2 sprints): run against synthetic scenarios and prior incidents; tune weights and cooldown curves.

Operational metrics to track:
- false_positive_rollbacks per 100 rollouts (target < 1/100)
- mean_time_to_detection for true regressions (target <= current baseline)
- percent of rollbacks where cost signal was primary veto (investigative)
- probe traffic cost overhead (target < 0.5% of canary cost)

Notes on privacy/compliance: probe payloads must not include customer PII. We'll sanitize prompts and run under existing KMS/HSM keys for auditability.
